name: Guests and waitlist
summary: Keeps the venue's guest waitlist in its own spreadsheet: puts each waiting party in order and quotes a wait from the minutes per group, logs every seated, no-show or left party once to a guest log, and queues the clearing of those rows for approval. Crons read and draft; a person approves every clear.

all.evidence: 1 hospitality discovery call names guests and waitlists; it describes no steps, so the steps below come from the kit's mapped operations and the walk-in pattern of the bookings workflow

covered_by.waitlist-add: skill (host adds a row with Status Waiting)
covered_by.record-keeping: close cron (guest log tab, once per party), queue cron (position and wait columns)
covered_by.other: skill (VIP handling, repeat guests, table choice, judged by hand)

crons.name: queue
crons.summary: Put each waiting party in order and quote its wait from minutes per group; mark rows it cannot read Check.

crons.name: close
crons.summary: Log each seated, no-show or left party once to the guest log; queue clearing those rows for approval (22:00 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia).

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: rows in the venue's own waitlist and guest log tabs. Clearing a waitlist row removes a record the host can see, so it is only ever queued for a person to approve. No cron messages a guest.

google-workspace.covers: waitlist rows, the guest log, and clearing a row after approval

gaps: Lightspeed: the kit has no Lightspeed ops file (core/sdk/platforms/lightspeed is absent), and its 28 pages are customer case studies with no waitlist, quote-wait, no-show or VIP flow. Nothing from it is built.

Guest notification when a table is ready (email or SMS): no mapped send operation with field names confirmed from the vendor spec is built. Gmail drafts are mapped in the kit, but no call describes this step, so it stays a later build.

Seating and table choice, no-show chasing, VIP or priority handling, repeat-guest lookup and marketing consent: no mapped platform describes them in the docs given. They are judgment steps in SKILL.md.
Walk-in and phone intake: no intake channel is mapped, so the host adds each row by hand.

Google Workspace: the customer-service and note-taking pages describe no waitlist, so the sheet is the only record. The adapter's field names come from the Sheets spec in endpoint-map/raw and it has not run against a real Google Workspace account.
The quoted wait is an estimate (minutes per group ahead in the queue), not a measured wait.

The clear re-reads the row before it runs, but the sheet drops empty cells at the end of a row, so an empty Note (or Outcome time) cannot be checked. A note typed into such an empty cell after queueing is cleared with the row. Check the row before approving a clear that has waited a long time.

evidence.calls: 1 hospitality discovery call mentions guests and waitlists (calls_read 1); it describes no steps, job types or volumes
evidence.platforms: google-workspace: partial for record-keeping (Sheets append, Google Docs notes); lightspeed: partial case-study mentions only, no mapped operations
